Plot Bayesian Quantitative Decision Regions

Source: R/f_plot_qtd_bayes.R
plot.TrialDesignPlanQuantitativeBayes.Rd

Displays decisions based on posterior criteria rather than frequentist intervals.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'TrialDesignPlanQuantitativeBayes'
plot(
  x,
  ...,
  type = 1L,
  estimates = NULL,
  standardErrors = 1,
  priorDist = NULL,
  estimateRange = c(-1, 2),
  standardErrorRange = c(0.1, 1),
  gridPoints = 50L,
  numberOfSubjects = NULL,
  priorDist1 = NULL,
  priorDist2 = NULL,
  directionUpper = TRUE,
  plotCat = 4L,
  main = "Bayesian quantitative decisions",
  plotSettings = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A Bayesian rule from getDesignQuantitative().

...

Additional arguments are checked for unknown names.

type

1 for observed effect estimates and posterior intervals, 2 for an effect-estimate/standard-error decision map, 3 for a binary count map.

estimates

Numeric vector of observed treatment-minus-control estimates for type 1.

standardErrors

Positive sampling standard errors, one per estimate or a common scalar. These describe effect estimates, not arm-level SDs.

priorDist

RBesT normMix effect prior for types 1 and 2. Defaults to mixnorm(c(1, 0, 100)). Group-mean priors are supported by the OC function; these effect-estimate plots require an effect prior.

estimateRange, standardErrorRange

Increasing two-element ranges for type 2.

gridPoints

Integer grid resolution per axis for type 2, at most 200.

numberOfSubjects

Positive integer vector (control, treatment) for type 3.

priorDist1, priorDist2

RBesT betaMix treatment and control priors for type 3.

directionUpper

Whether increasing treatment rates are beneficial.

plotCat

Three or four decision categories.

main

Plot title.

plotSettings

Optional PlotSettings object.

Value

A ggplot object containing the evaluated decisions in its data.

Details

Type 1 shows equal-tail 95 percent posterior intervals for orientation; categories always use the actual posterior criteria, not these display bounds. Exact posterior probability-threshold ties belong to Indeterminate 2. Type 3 uses the same full posterior decision grid as binary OCs. The grid contains at most one million cells; large grids can be expensive to evaluate.

See also

getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans(), getOperatingCharacteristicsRates()
